title: Pair packed-support decoding with canonical block materialization attribution
question: After GPU-12 fused repeated CSR validation scans and GPU-13 isolated exact Boolean scalar admission, how expensive is the existing packed-support-to-CSR decoder relative to the unchanged canonical TypedRelationBlock constructor on the same frozen Fourfold cases?

change.profiler_schema: Bump the existing contained TypedRelationBlock validation profiler from /2 to /3 instead of creating a new benchmark harness.
change.support_decode_timing: Measure the exact existing experiments.tensor_gpu.cpu_bitset_baseline._csr_support_from_masks path with the same warmup/repeat policy used by scalar admission and canonical construction.
change.semantic_control: Require deterministic support re-decoding and require the canonical block row_offsets/column_indices plus digest to match the decoded support on every profiled case.
change.comparison: Report support-decode/constructor and scalar/constructor ratios only from independently sampled medians; explicitly retain the non-additivity caveat.
change.test_contract: Pin schema /3, exact existing decoder reuse, support entry parity, common sampling policy, ratio fields, fail-closed scalar semantics, and the no-structural-bypass boundary.

verification.matrix: Python 3.10/3.12 x PYTHONHASHSEED 0/123456 integrated contract jobs succeeded
verification.designated_python_312_hash0: compile, integrated contract surface, packed CPU baseline, TypedRelationBlock materialization profile /3, residency diagnostic, fanout diagnostic, artifact uploads, and public package API verification succeeded

frozen_support_decode_diagnostic.measurement_caveat: Support decode, scalar admission, and canonical constructor are independently sampled operations and are not additive. Hosted-run timings are diagnostic only and are not a general performance claim.

finding.summary: Packed-support decoding is already comparable to the entire canonical block constructor on the larger frozen cases: 0.932x to 0.976x of constructor median for 128/0.05, 256/0.01, and 256/0.05. Scalar admission remains material but smaller at about 0.35x to 0.39x of constructor median there.
finding.negative_result: The evidence does not justify optimizing only TypedRelationBlock.__post_init__, adding a trusted constructor, or adding a cache/backend abstraction. Even a hypothetical free constructor would leave an almost equally large packed-support-to-CSR decoding boundary on larger outputs.
finding.next_implication: The next narrow experiment should test whether packed rows can materialize canonical CSR support with fewer Python-level per-set-bit operations while preserving exact sorted support and MAX_BLOCK_ENTRIES refusal, before any production-path change.
